title: Hackers now scanning systems for recently-patched Oracle flaw
content_md: Attackers have begun probing the Internet for systems unpatched against a recently disclosed critical Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS) vulnerability. Discovered in a core component of EBS's Application Object Library and tracked as CVE-2026-101767 , this flaw lets unauthenticated threat actors with HTTP network access take over vulnerable systems in low-complexity attacks. Oracle released security updates to address the issue in its October 2026 Critical Security Patch Update on October 20 and urged customers to patch their systems immediately. "In some instances, it has been reported that attackers have been successful because targeted customers had failed to apply available Oracle patches," it said. "Oracle therefore strongly recommends that customers remain on actively-supported versions and apply security patches without delay." While Oracle has not yet tagged CVE-2026-101767 as exploited in the wild, threat intelligence company Defused said on Tuesday that it already spotted threat actors scanning the Internet for vulnerable systems. "Our Oracle E-Business Suite decoys recorded exploratory exploits against CVE-2026-101767, an unauthenticated SQL injection in EBS's Thin Client Framework servlet that chains to remote code execution, this morning, Oct 27," Defused warned . ​Internet threat watchdog Shadowserver now tracks over 670 Internet-exposed Oracle EBS instances , most of them with IP addresses from the United States.
